clue.text: People's right to enjoy something -- a policy abandoned by New Labour?

definitions.text: a policy abandoned by New Labour

blocks.note: first meaning: something held in common by the whole people

blocks.clueFragment: a policy abandoned by New Labour
blocks.note: second meaning: the nationalisation commitment in Clause IV, dropped by Tony Blair's party in 1995

explanation.walkthrough: New Labour was Tony Blair's rebranded British Labour Party, which rewrote Clause IV of its constitution to remove the nationalisation pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: State control of industry for the nation's benefit is both a collective right of citizens and the socialist programme Blair discarded.

clue.text: Fine gunfight, or sudden death on the draw?

blocks.note: a fine is a monetary punishment
a gun battle, as in a Western

explanation.surface: A Wild West duel: a gunfight where someone falls dead the instant pistols are drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the draw' sounds like drawing a gun, but here it means after a drawn football match.
explanation.definitionFit: When a knockout football match ends level, players take alternate kicks at goal until one side wins, a decisive tiebreak.

clue.text: Rabelaisian wife replaces daughter in villain's heart

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means a letter is swapped out for a new one
the heart is the centre, so the swap happens in the middle of the word

blocks.note: a baddy is the villain of a story
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A domestic melodrama in which the villain's affections shift from his daughter to his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' points to the middle of the five letters, where one D gives way to W.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabelais wrote earthy, ribald comic tales, so Rabelaisian describes humour that is coarse, lewd and indecent.

clue.text: He has sex appeal and a half lira -- an Umbrian, perhaps?

indicators.note: taking half of a word keeps only two of its four letters, here the front pair

blocks.note: 'it' is an old term for sex appeal
taken as written
the front two of the currency's four letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A charming man with sex appeal but only half a lira to his name, probably from central Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a region of central Italy, so anyone from there is an example of a native of that country.

clue.text: Stormy Skye or N. Scottish isles

indicators.note: a storm throws things into turmoil, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: letters taken as written; N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A weather report: storms over Skye or the islands of northern Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is a real Scottish island, so it seems to belong to the definition, but it is all anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: The archipelago off the northern tip of mainland Scotland is a group of islands, so the plural form fits.

clue.text: Lunatic can't sue after shock treatment

indicators.note: a shock jolts things out of place, so the letters emerge rearranged

blocks.note: letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A mental patient, given electroconvulsive therapy, is told he has no right to take legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal nouns for a crazy person, someone mad or wildly eccentric.

clue.text: Renaissance man, BBC boss, involved in getting her back

indicators.note: getting something back here means reading the word from its end to its start
being involved in something puts one item inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
John Birt was Director-General of the BBC in the 1990s

explanation.surface: A cultured BBC chief, a true Renaissance man, is caught up in winning back a lost love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renaissance man' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at Renaissance; the BBC is Britain's public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Renaissance literally means being born again, a revival or renewal of something.

clue.text: Biochemical released in allergic reaction with a rich supply after this is injured

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
one part coming after another fixes which piece is placed first

blocks.note: letters taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written
a mine is a rich source, as in a mine of information

explanation.surface: A medical description of the chemistry of an allergic attack after an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: This compound is released by mast cells during allergies, causing swelling and itching, which antihistamine drugs block.

clue.text: Immersed in ancient writing, little George makes a study of the Old World

definitions.text: a study of the Old World

indicators.note: something immersed in a liquid sits inside it, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: the study of old handwriting and manuscripts
a shortening of the name

explanation.surface: A boy named George, lost in old manuscripts, becomes a scholar of ancient history.
explanation.definitionFit: This science reconstructs the geography of past geological ages, the layout of continents and seas in a former world.

clue.text: Original place for selling races

blocks.note: new and original both mean novel
a market is where goods are sold

explanation.surface: A historical note about where selling first took place.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is a town in Suffolk, England, famous as the home of British horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The racecourse town is used for the meetings held there, just as Ascot or Epsom names its horse-racing events.

clue.text: A degree to little Sarah is fundamental

blocks.note: a Bachelor of Arts is a degree
Sal is a pet form of Sarah

explanation.surface: Awarding a university degree to young Sarah is of key importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe what forms the base or foundation of something, its most essential layer.

clue.text: Magical connection between parts of a landscape in part of an old poem, read out loud

definitions.text: Magical connection between parts of a landscape

indicators.note: words read out loud are heard rather than seen, so their sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a lay is an old narrative poem, and a line is one part of it

explanation.surface: A folklorist reads aloud a verse describing mystical links between landmarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient sites are said by enthusiasts to align along straight tracks carrying mysterious earth energy, an alleged supernatural link.

clue.text: Expose craze for bad behaviour on planes

blocks.note: to air something is to make it public
a rage is a fashion, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: A newspaper campaign to expose the trend of passengers behaving badly in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the established term for violent or abusive conduct by passengers during a flight.

clue.text: Wily Estonian keeps an agreement

indicators.note: a phrase that keeps something holds it inside, so the letters lie within these words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A cunning man from Estonia holds on to a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word is an affirmative reply, an act of consent or assent.

clue.text: Underpants? Heard why they face the sea?

indicators.note: something heard is taken by ear, so the sound of the word counts

blocks.note: the letter's name is said the same as the question word
seafronts are the promenades facing the sea

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about underwear and seaside promenades.
explanation.walkthrough: Y-fronts are British men's briefs with an upside-down Y-shaped seam at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade name for a style of men's briefs is used as a general noun for that type of undergarment.

clue.text: Liking for ceremony involving rum: it is all endless!

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter of the last word is cut off
involving here means tangling together, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: A drinker's toast at a ceremonial occasion: rum is everything, without limit!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like an anagram signal, meaning strange, but it is part of the material to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The ism names an excessive devotion to ritual, a fondness for formal religious ceremonial.

clue.text: Rubbish found in vegetation

indicators.note: something found in a word lies within its letters

blocks.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: Litter discovered among the plants and undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe cheap, worthless or shoddy goods, junk of poor quality.

clue.text: Repeating what others have said: choir has no right to be in England

indicators.note: having no right means losing the abbreviation for right from the word
being in something puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: ENG is the abbreviation for England
the choir without R, the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cathedral choir is told it has no right to perform in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo someone is to repeat their words or opinions, parroting what was said before.

clue.text: Leaders of Champagne region unions formed vineyard

indicators.note: the leaders of a group are those at its front, so each word's opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Trade unions in the Champagne district have joined together to create a vineyard.
explanation.definitionFit: In French wine terms a cru is a vineyard or a wine of recognised quality, as in grand cru.

clue.text: Fresh marijuana's in these casseroles

blocks.note: hot as in hot off the press, newly made
pot is slang for marijuana, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A warning that someone has slipped cannabis into the stews.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lancashire hotpot is a British stew of lamb and onion topped with sliced potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: These slow-baked meat and vegetable stews are a kind of casserole, cooked in a covered dish.

clue.text: Folding paper round equipment and a note

blocks.note: O is round in shape
a rig is a set of equipment
the a taken as written
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Wrapping paper folded around a gadget, with a little note attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folding paper' reads as a noun phrase for a type of paper, but it means the act of folding paper.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese art involves creasing sheets of paper into decorative shapes without cutting or gluing.

clue.text: She, after he has left, is tied to doorpost by consent to get the rhino whip!

indicators.note: once he has left, those two letters depart from the word

blocks.note: the word with its last two letters removed
a jamb is the side post of a door frame
OK signals agreement

explanation.surface: A melodrama: her man gone, a woman is bound to the doorpost and, with her agreement, whipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A sjambok is a heavy South African whip traditionally made of rhinoceros or hippopotamus hide.

clue.text: Nothing's chasing U-boat when it's freezing cold

indicators.note: a chaser comes behind what it pursues, so this piece goes second

blocks.note: a U-boat is a German submarine
zero is nothing

explanation.surface: A wartime chase: nothing pursues the German submarine through icy waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperatures below the freezing point of water are extremely cold, below nought on the Celsius scale.

clue.text: Support old and new British cheese

blocks.note: a stilt is a post supporting a building
O is the abbreviation for old
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A customer at a cheese counter backing both aged and young British cheeses.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a famous English blue-veined cheese, a classic example of British cheesemaking.

clue.text: Plead for British cheese, for a change

indicators.note: making a change alters the order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
letters taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone begging for British cheese as a welcome variation in diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to beg or implore someone urgently, an earnest appeal.

clue.text: Stick out by a small margin, but less small

indicators.note: less means minus, so the abbreviation for small is removed

blocks.note: just, as in just made it
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Something protrudes only slightly, then a little less.
explanation.definitionFit: To jut is to project or protrude beyond the surrounding surface.

clue.text: Variation in C: air on a wind instrument

indicators.note: a musical variation reworks a theme, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A concert programme: variations on an air in C major, played on a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This small egg-shaped flute of clay with finger holes is a woodwind played by blowing.

clue.text: I approach new, more reliable underwriter

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
surer means more certain or dependable

explanation.surface: A customer turning to a new, more trustworthy insurance company.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwriter is someone who accepts liability for a risk in return for a premium, the role of a cover provider.

clue.text: Greyhound, for instance, runs round one

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run, so two of them
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A greyhound sprinting round the track for one lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like the verb for what the greyhound does; it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A greyhound is bred for speed on a track, an example of an animal that competes in races.

clue.text: Board has approval from the French and the Germans

blocks.note: the French word for yes
the German word for yes

explanation.surface: A company board wins the support of both French and German partners.
explanation.walkthrough: The name joins the French and German words for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: This lettered board is used at seances to receive supposed messages from spirits.

clue.text: Bert cut up wild flower

indicators.note: something wild is uncontrolled, so the letters are let loose into a new order

blocks.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Bert snipped a wildflower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' looks like the anagram signal and 'wild flower' like the definition; 'cut up' is fodder and 'wild' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow meadow plant of the ranunculus family is a common example of a bloom.

clue.text: A prostitute, a detective and a prince - all just regular folk

blocks.note: tom is British slang for a prostitute
dick is slang for a detective, as in private dick
taken as written
Prince Harry of the British royal family

explanation.surface: A list of an unlikely trio, a sex worker, a sleuth and a royal, declared to be ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names everyone and anyone, ordinary people in general rather than anybody special.
